edges.description: Defective chemotaxis, shear-dependent L-selectin capture, F-actin generation, and p38 and p42/p44 MAP kinase activation.
edges.limitations: A complete null, whereas the human disease is caused by a heterozygous dominant-negative allele that poisons the wild-type product. The endpoints converge but the genetic mechanisms differ, so the model cannot speak to dominant-negative sequestration itself. Superoxide production was reduced in bone marrow neutrophils but NORMAL in activated peritoneal exudate neutrophils, so the oxidase arm is only partially reproduced and that node is deliberately not claimed.

edges.description: Supplies a mechanism for the peripheral neutrophilia that the entry otherwise curates only as an observation: RAC2 is required for CXCR4-mediated RETENTION of neutrophils in haematopoietic tissue, so losing it increases mobilization into the circulation. Neutrophilia is therefore not merely a failure to consume neutrophils at tissue sites - it is partly an active over-release.
edges.limitations: The retention finding is established in zebrafish haematopoietic tissue, which is not anatomically equivalent to human bone marrow, and the rescue experiment that demonstrates it uses a CXCR4 gain-of-function background from a different disease.

nodes.description: The second effector arm, and the one chronic granulomatous disease does not have. Patient neutrophils show decreased chemotaxis, polarization and azurophilic granule secretion. In the Rac2-null mouse the same arm fails through defective F-actin generation, impaired p38 and p42/p44 MAP kinase activation, and loss of shear-dependent L-selectin-mediated capture, so the defect spans capture, polarization and migration rather than any single step. This is curated as a separate node from the oxidase arm rather than bundled into one "neutrophil dysfunction" node, because the two are independent effector routes from the same GTPase.

evidence.snippet: Neutrophils from this patient exhibited decreased chemotaxis, polarization, azurophilic granule secretion, and superoxide anion (O(2)(-)) production but had normal expression and up-regulation of CD11b.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the hematopoietic cell-specific Rho family GTPase Rac2 is characterized by abnormalities in neutrophil function and host defense.
evidence.snippet: rac2-/- neutrophils displayed significant defects in chemotaxis, in shear-dependent L-selectin-mediated capture on the endothelial substrate Glycam-1, and in both F-actin generation and p38 and, unexpectedly, p42/p44 MAP kinase activation induced by chemoattractants.

nodes.description: The first of the two effector arms. RAC2 is required for activation of the NOX2 NADPH oxidase, and the D57N protein inhibits oxidase activation in vitro. The defect is at the level of the ACTIVATOR, not the catalytic complex, which is what distinguishes this from chronic granulomatous disease even though the downstream consequence - failed respiratory burst - is shared. The decisive reconstitution experiment is that adding recombinant Rac to patient neutrophil extracts restores superoxide production.

evidence.reference_title: Human neutrophil immunodeficiency syndrome is associated with an inhibitory Rac2 mutation.
evidence.snippet: Addition of recombinant Rac to extracts of the patient neutrophils reconstituted O(2)(-) production in an in vitro assay system.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and functional spectrum of RAC2-related immunodeficiency.
evidence.snippet: Most mutants produced elevated superoxide; mutations unable to support superoxide formation were associated with bacterial infections.

nodes.description: The definitive therapy. RAC2 is expressed only in haematopoietic cells, so replacing the haematopoietic compartment replaces the entire diseased tissue - there is no other organ carrying the lesion. In the RAC2 cohort most patients with dominant-negative disease were transplanted within the first year of life.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and functional spectrum of RAC2-related immunodeficiency.
evidence.snippet: Most patients with constitutively active and DN disease underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) within the first months (constitutively active) to first year (DN D57N) of life

nodes.description: The two arms converge here, and the convergence explains the syndrome's most distinctive feature: peripheral neutrophilia coexisting with an absence of neutrophils where they are needed. Neutrophils are produced and released normally but do not accumulate at infected sites, so infections proceed without pus formation and wounds heal poorly. The Rac2-null mouse reproduces exactly this pairing - baseline neutrophilia in the blood alongside reduced inflammatory peritoneal exudate.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the hematopoietic cell-specific Rho family GTPase Rac2 is characterized by abnormalities in neutrophil function and host defense.
evidence.snippet: These defects were reflected in vivo by baseline neutrophilia, reduced inflammatory peritoneal exudate formation, and increased mortality when challenged with Aspergillus fumigatus.

meta.association: The dominant-negative p.Asp57Asn allele, arising from a G to A change at nucleotide 169 of the coding sequence. Asp57 is invariant in all defined GTP-binding proteins and is directly involved in nucleotide binding.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant negative mutation of the hematopoietic-specific Rho GTPase, Rac2, is associated with a human phagocyte immunodeficiency.
evidence.snippet: Molecular methods were used to clone the expressed Rac2 cDNA from this patient, and a single base pair change (G-->A at nucleotide 169) in the coding sequence was identified. This results in an asparagine for aspartic acid mutation at amino acid 57 (D57N), a residue that is involved in nucleotide binding and is conserved in all mammalian Rho GTPases.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion. Asp57 is invariant across GTP-binding proteins and participates directly in nucleotide binding. The mutant protein binds GDP but not GTP, so it is locked in the inactive conformation, and it acts dominant-negatively rather than as a simple null: it sequesters guanine nucleotide exchange factors and effectors away from the wild-type protein. That is why one allele is enough.

evidence.reference_title: Human neutrophil immunodeficiency syndrome is associated with an inhibitory Rac2 mutation.
evidence.snippet: Asp57 is invariant in all defined GTP-binding proteins. Rac2(D57N) binds GDP but not GTP and inhibits oxidase activation and O(2)(-) production in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant negative mutation of the hematopoietic-specific Rho GTPase, Rac2, is associated with a human phagocyte immunodeficiency.
evidence.snippet: Functional studies demonstrated that the D57N mutant behaves in a dominant-negative fashion at the cellular level.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous germline p.Asp57Asn. The functional impact is recorded as DOMINANT_NEGATIVE rather than LOSS_OF_FUNCTION because the mutant actively inhibits the wild-type allele's product; a heterozygous null at this locus does not produce the disease.

nodes.description: Reproduces the defining paradox of the human disease - neutrophilia in blood with failure to form a tissue exudate - and resolves the migration arm into capture, actin assembly and MAP kinase components.

The only available model carrying the actual human allele this entry is scoped to, rather than a null. That distinction matters: the mouse knockout models absence of the protein, while this model expresses the same dominant-negative protein patients carry, and so speaks to the sequestration mechanism the null cannot address. Expressing D57N in neutrophils alone is sufficient to produce the immunodeficiency phenotype, which localises the disease to the neutrophil rather than to some broader haematopoietic effect.

The clinical presentation, in the index case at five weeks of age. Routine screening tests are normal, so the diagnosis is easily missed: the neutrophil count is high rather than low, CD11b is normal, and the defect is functional rather than numerical.
